10.  Council Comments  Council Member Crosby stated he was very pleased with the reopening of the
  restaurants and he fully appreciated and thanked City staff for assisting the
  downtown businesses on the closure of" D" Street befinreen Third Street and
  Bonita Avenue. He urged everyone to get vaccinated and to help those
  individuals to get vaccinated.  He was pleased with the sales tax report.

  Council Member Lau also was very pleased with the reopening of the
  restaurants.  She also urged everyone to get vaccinated; keep social
  distancing,  and  wear masks to stay safe. She reported on the University of
  La Verne' s winter graduation.

  Council Member Davis also urged residents to help those who need to get
  vaccinated.

  Mayor Pro Tem Carder also stated that she was happy with downtown
  La Verne restaurants reopening; but reminded everyone not to forget the
  Foothill Corridor restaurants  and  businesses.  She reported on the Gold Line
  Construction Project and that the intersection of Wheeler and Arrow Highway
  is now open.

  Mayor Hepburn thanked City Manager Russi, Interim Public Works Director
  Keesey and his staff for all their work in assisting the downtown business by
  closing " D" Street. He reminded everyone to shop La Verne and not to forget
  about the Foothill Corridor restaurants and shops. He urged residents to get

  vaccinated, wear your masks and to stay safe.

 City of La Verne Council Meeting Feb. 1, 2021-- Public Comment

Good evening Council Members, Mr Russi

I wish to address the need for a public vote on the issue regarding contracting with LACFD for
Fire Suppression and Emergency Medical Response Services.

I have always held a high regard for how the City of La Verne has handled its business publicly in
a very transparent manner.

However,  in this instance there seems to be a less than transparent  public approach  to this
contract  proposal.  The City has posted to the City' s website the LACFD Feasibility
  Messina&  Associates Report, and a report generated
Study/ Contract Proposal along with  the

by the City Staff regarding this issue. But the total financial impact to the City' s finances has not
been presented in clear and understandable terms.

The first 10 years of the contract would cost the City approximately 7. 5 million dollars more
than  maintaining LVFD.  Plus, the loss of approx. 700 thousand  dollars per year in medical
insurance reimbursement to the City for Rescue Ambulance transportation, which would
instead go  to  private  ambulance  service.  The 10 year loss of revenue on that alone amounts to
7 million  dollars.  For the 10 year contract with LACFD the City would suffer a 14. 5 million dollar
revenue( oss by contracting with LACFD.

The second 10 year contract would cost the City 85. 5 million dollars more than maintaining
LVFD, plus the loss of an additional 7 million dollars in insurance reimbursement.

Over the next 20 years it would cost the City 107 million dollars over what it would cost to
maintain LVFD, and Station 3 would never be operational again resulting in much longer
response times by Fire and Emergency Medical Response to North La Verne.

The LACFD contract proposal is grossly overpriced and delivers a much less quality service level
for Emergency Medical Response for all La Verne residents.

We cannot continue to deal effectively with this issue with the limiting opportunities for public
input on Zoom  media.  This issue needs much more public in person discussion due to the
extreme  financial  impact  of this proposal.

Please discontinue further negotiations with LACFD until we can have in person public
discussion on the financial impact and the reduction of other City services that will result.
